Why you should not use elevators during an earthquake
ET Online
Mar 22, 2023
Elevators may malfunction
Elevators are powered by electricity and can be susceptible to damage or malfunction during an earthquake, which could leave you trapped inside.
Image Source: iStock
Shaking may damage elevator machinery
The intense shaking of an earthquake can damage elevator machinery or break elevator cables, causing the elevator to drop or become stuck between floors.
Image Source: iStock
Hazards inside the elevator
During an earthquake, there may be power outages or other hazards such as falling debris or fires that can further endanger those inside the elevator.
Image Source: iStock
Difficulty of rescue
Emergency services may not be able to reach you quickly if you are trapped inside an elevator, as they will be prioritizing more urgent situations.
Image Source: iStock
Stairs are a safer option
Once it is safe to do so, using the stairs to evacuate the building is a safer option than relying on the elevator, as stairs are typically more stable and less likely to be affected by power outages or other issues during an earthquake.
Image Source: iStock
Other things to avoid
​Here are the other things to avoid during an earthquake.
Image Source: iStock
Don't panic
Although earthquakes can be scary, it's important to try to remain calm and focused. Panic can lead to poor decision-making, which can increase your risk of injury or harm.
Image Source: iStock
​Don't stand under a doorway
Contrary to popular belief, standing under a doorway is not necessarily the safest place to be during an earthquake. In modern buildings, doorways are no stronger than any other part of the building and may not provide adequate protection from falling debris or objects.
Image Source: iStock
Don't run outside
While it might seem like the safest option to run outside, it's important to remember that many injuries during earthquakes happen when people try to leave buildings or move around. If you're indoors, stay there until the shaking stops.
Image Source: iStock
